note: Formula/equation cards. Facts are from the cited NCERT section. Mnemonics are Red Pen memory aids (NOT from NCERT) and are a low-utility helper per Dunlosky et al. 2013; testing yourself works better.

items.title: Law of conservation of mass
items.body: Total mass of reactants = total mass of products. So the number of atoms of each element must be equal on both sides: balance the equation.

items.title: Combination reaction
items.body: A + B -> AB. Example: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + heat (quicklime + water = slaked lime).

items.title: Decomposition reactions
items.body: One reactant -> two or more products. Heat: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2. Electricity: 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2 (H2 : O2 = 2 : 1). Light: 2AgCl -> 2Ag + Cl2.
items.mnemonic: Decomposition needs energy: Heat, Light or Electricity (HLE).

items.title: Displacement reaction
items.body: A more reactive element displaces a less reactive one: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu.

items.title: Double displacement
items.body: AB + CD -> AD + CB. Example: Na2SO4 + BaCl2 -> BaSO4 (white ppt) + 2NaCl.

items.title: Oxidation and reduction (Class 10 view)
items.body: Oxidation = gain of oxygen / loss of hydrogen. Reduction = loss of oxygen / gain of hydrogen. Both happen together (redox): CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O.
items.mnemonic: Oxygen In = Oxidation. Hydrogen In = Reduction.

items.title: Acid + metal
items.body: Acid + metal -> salt + hydrogen gas. Zn + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2 (pops with a burning candle).

items.title: Acid + metal carbonate / hydrogencarbonate
items.body: Acid + metal carbonate -> salt + CO2 + H2O. CO2 turns lime water milky: Ca(OH)2 + CO2 -> CaCO3 + H2O.

items.title: Neutralisation
items.body: Acid + base -> salt + water. NaOH + HCl -> NaCl + H2O.

items.title: pH scale
items.body: 0 to 14. pH 7 neutral, below 7 acidic, above 7 basic. Lower pH = stronger acid (more H+).
items.mnemonic: 7 is neutral; less than 7 = Sour side (acid).

items.title: Baking soda and washing soda
items.body: Baking soda: NaHCO3. 2NaHCO3 -(heat)-> Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2. Washing soda: Na2CO3.10H2O.

items.title: Chlor-alkali process
items.body: 2NaCl + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + Cl2 + H2 (electrolysis of brine).

items.title: Plaster of Paris
items.body: Gypsum CaSO4.2H2O, heated at 373 K, gives plaster of Paris CaSO4.1/2H2O.

items.title: Reactivity series (NCERT list)
items.body: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au (most to least reactive).
items.mnemonic: Kabhi Naa Calm Mat Aao, Zara Ferry Pe Hum, Cute Hathi Aur Aadmi  (K Na Ca Mg Al Zn Fe Pb H Cu Hg Ag Au)

items.title: Amphoteric oxides
items.body: Al2O3 and ZnO react with both acids and bases: Al2O3 + 6HCl -> 2AlCl3 + 3H2O ; Al2O3 + 2NaOH -> 2NaAlO2 + H2O.

items.title: Thermit reaction
items.body: Fe2O3 + 2Al -> 2Fe + Al2O3 + heat (used to join railway tracks).

items.title: Roasting and calcination
items.body: Roasting (sulphide ore in air): 2ZnS + 3O2 -> 2ZnO + 2SO2. Calcination (carbonate ore, limited air): ZnCO3 -> ZnO + CO2. Then ZnO + C -> Zn + CO.
items.mnemonic: Roasting = sulphide + lots of air; Calcination = carbonate + little air.

items.title: Electrolytic refining and extraction
items.body: Cathode: Na+ + e- -> Na (metal deposits). Anode: 2Cl- -> Cl2 + 2e-. Highly reactive metals (above Al) are extracted by electrolysis of molten salts.

items.title: Rusting needs air AND water
items.body: Iron + oxygen + moisture -> rust. Prevent by painting, oiling, galvanisation (zinc coat), alloying.

items.title: Hydrocarbon general formulas
items.body: Alkane CnH2n+2, alkene CnH2n, alkyne CnH2n-2. Example n=2: ethane C2H6, ethene C2H4, ethyne C2H2.
items.mnemonic: Alkane = all single (n, 2n+2); alkEne has a double; alkYne has a triple (fewer H each time).

items.title: Homologous series
items.body: Same functional group; successive members differ by -CH2- (12+2 = 14 u). Similar chemical properties, gradual change in physical properties.

items.title: Combustion
items.body: Carbon compound + O2 -> CO2 + H2O + heat + light. CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O.

items.title: Reactions of ethanol
items.body: 2C2H5OH + 2Na -> 2C2H5ONa + H2. Hot conc. H2SO4 at 443 K: C2H5OH -> CH2=CH2 + H2O (dehydration).

items.title: Esterification and saponification
items.body: Ethanoic acid + ethanol (conc. H2SO4) -> ester (sweet smell) + water. Ester + NaOH -> alcohol + sodium salt of the acid (soap).

items.title: Addition reaction
items.body: Unsaturated + H2 (nickel catalyst) -> saturated: CH2=CH2 + H2 -> CH3-CH3. Used to turn vegetable oils into fats.

items.title: Ethanoic acid reactions
items.body: CH3COOH + NaHCO3 -> CH3COONa + H2O + CO2. Also reacts with Na and NaOH like a (weak) acid.
